title: The Borrow Shed
intro: Text 1 is a webpage for a tool-lending cupboard run by the residents of a housing block.

visual.text: THE BORROW SHED · VOID DECK, BLOCK 318
You need a hole in the wall, not a drill in the cupboard.
Borrow the tool. Finish the job. Bring it back.
A cupboard under a staircase with open doors, showing rows of drills, ladders and spanners, each with a numbered tag. A handwritten sign on the door reads ‘Take what you need. Return what you took.’

Most tools in a home are used for a few minutes a year and spend the rest of their lives gathering dust. The Borrow Shed is a shared cupboard run by residents, for residents. Borrow a ladder to change a light bulb, a pump for your bicycle, or a sewing machine to hem new curtains — free, for up to three days.

visual.title: Three steps
items: Scan the tag on the tool with your phone
Take it home and use it with care
Wipe it clean and hang it back on the same hook

visual.text: “My son wanted to build a shelf for a school project. We borrowed a saw and a sander, and the uncle on duty spent half an hour showing him how to use them safely.” — Mrs Kaur, Block 320
See what is on the shelves today
Have a tool you never use? Donate it and let it work for the whole block.

text2.intro: Text 2 is taken from a residents’ newsletter article about one of the volunteers at the Borrow Shed.
paragraphs: Mr Tan, a retired aircraft technician of 68, spends two evenings a week beside the cupboard under the stairs. ‘People think I am here to guard the tools,’ he laughs. ‘Actually, I am here to talk.’ Nearly everything on the shelves was given by neighbours. ‘When people donate, they always tell me the same thing: they bought it for one job years ago and never touched it again.’

What surprises him most is who comes to borrow. It is not only fathers fixing taps, but teenagers building projects and grandmothers hanging photo frames. ‘Last week a boy came for a saw and stayed an hour asking me how planes stay up,’ he says. ‘The tools are the excuse. The shed is really about knowing your neighbours.’

questions.text: Look at the picture in Text 1. How does it support the tagline ‘Borrow the tool. Finish the job. Bring it back.’?

scheme.answer: Each tool has a numbered tag and the sign tells people to return what they took, which shows the tools are shared and are meant to come back after use.
accept: The rows of tagged tools and the sign on the door show a shared cupboard where you take a tool and put it back, as the tagline says.

seeds.text: The tools all have number tags and the sign on the door says to return what you took, so it shows the tools are for everyone to borrow and then bring back, like the tagline.
The handwritten sign and the tags show that you can take a tool but must put it back, which matches borrowing it and returning it.
It shows that the tools are being sold cheaply to residents.
It shows a cupboard with a lot of tools.
A cupboard under a staircase with open doors.
